title: Preemptive request priority bench scratchpad (Anna)
content:
Notes / hypothesis:
- Goal: understand impact of preemptive priority handling on latency and throughput under mixed workloads. We allow high-priority (HP) LLM requests to preempt low-priority (LP) requests already queued/executing on the same GPU.
- Hypothesis: preemption reduces HP tail latency but may increase LP p99 and reduce aggregate throughput due to wasted compute/kv-cache churn.

Test matrix (quick):
- Model: llama-70B-quant (fp16 fallback path enabled)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 for LP; HP always batch=1
- Workload mixes: HP:LP = 0:100, 5:95, 10:90, 20:80, 50:50 by qps
- QPS targets: total 100 qps and 400 qps (two load regimes)
- Preemption modes: off (baseline FIFO), soft-preempt (drain after token), hard-preempt (kill & reschedule)
- Cache state: cold vs warm KV cache
- Duration: steady 10m per run after 2m warmup

Environment:
- Dedicated test GPU: a100-40GB x1 (single GPU) on dev cluster-redwood-qa-3
- Serving runtime build: runtime@pr-842 (sched:preemptive-experiment)
- Client harness: bench-client v0.12 (jittered inter-arrival, 95th percentile bursty source)
- Metrics collectors: prometheus scrape interval 15s, perf counters at 1s, runtime traces enabled (sampling 1/1000)

Commands used (harness snippets):
- bench-client --target-host runtime.qa.redwood:443 --model llama-70b-quant --concurrency 200 --qps 400 --mix "hp=40,lp=360" --priority-map "hp:high,lp:low" --duration 12m
- curl admin/runtime/metrics?include_gpu=true

Raw aggregated results (selected runs) - total QPS=400, cache warm, batch LP=4:
- Baseline (no preempt): HP p50=42ms p95=120ms p99=280ms; LP p50=45ms p95=135ms p99=310ms; aggregate throughput=396 qps; GPU util=92%
- Soft-preempt: HP p50=28ms p95=60ms p99=140ms; LP p50=48ms p95=210ms p99=820ms; aggregate throughput=376 qps; GPU util=85%
- Hard-preempt: HP p50=22ms p95=48ms p99=95ms; LP p50=52ms p95=420ms p99=>1200ms (many timeouts); aggregate throughput=310 qps; GPU util=73%

Observations:
1) HP latency improved a lot with either preempt mode (esp hard-preempt). p99 for HP dropped ~3x vs baseline. Good for SLOs that prioritize HP.
2) LP tail latency skyrocketed, especially under hard-preempt where many LP requests were killed mid-execution and retried causing amplification. p99 > 1s in some runs; many client-level timeouts triggered.
3) Aggregate throughput drops significantly in hard-preempt mode: wasted cycles from killed LP work + increased scheduling churn. Soft-preempt traded some LP tail for better throughput than hard.
4) GPU util dropped as preemption aggressiveness increased. This is likely due to context-switch gaps and reupload/kv-cache misses from restart.
5) Warm KV cache helps reduce absolute latencies but doesn't change relative pattern: preemption still causes LP regression.

Quick micro-profiling notes:
- When preempt triggers: we see ~10-40ms scheduling gap (tensor free/realloc) per preempt event.
- KV cache invalidation: hard-preempt yields frequent KV cache misses on resumed LP jobs -> extra ~60-120ms penalty per restart.
- PCIe transfers spiked when killed job had partially materialized attention caches -> system had to re-stream for retried LP.

Trade-offs + implications:
- If customers require strict HP SLOs (e.g., interactive assistant), hard-preempt might be acceptable if LP traffic is best-effort and we can surface timeouts/SLAs.
- For mixed-tenant clusters, hard preempt harms overall efficiency and increases cost per effective token.
- Soft-preempt (drain at token boundary) is a good compromise: HP latency improves substantially while limiting rework.

Mitigations to explore:
- Preemption budget per LP request: allow up to X tokens before forced preempt to reduce wasted compute.
- Checkpoint lightweight KV cache per request so restart can resume without full penalty. (trade memory)
- Backpressure earlier in stack: deny admission of new LP requests when HP qps above threshold instead of preempting running LPs.
- Prefer slot-based isolation for a fraction of GPUs for HP burst capacity instead of preemption on every GPU.

Action items / next runs:
- A1: Run soft-preempt with preempt-token-budget = 8 tokens, LP batch size sweep [1,2,4,8] at total QPS=400. (Assign: Evan)
- A2: Measure retry amplification effect: instrument client retries to distinguish restarted LP vs fresh. (Assign: me)
- A3: Prototype a tiny KV checkpoint (in-memory) per request and re-run hard-preempt to measure penalty delta. (Assign: Samir)
- A4: Run same matrix on 2xA100 multi-GPU to see if preemption impact is less on distributed execution.

Open questions / notes to think about:
- What is acceptable LP degradation for customers? Need product input. Add to product backlog.
- Are there simple heuristics to prefer preempting the smallest LP jobs first? (size-aware preempt)
- Cost model: quantify wasted token-op cost vs HP SLA benefit.

Scratch data snippets (for record):
- Sample timeline (soft-preempt run, HP:LP=10:90, total qps=100):
  - t=0-120s warmup, t=120s enable preempt, HP p99 drops from 340ms -> 130ms over next 60s
  - LP p99 rises from 360ms -> 700ms; error rate increased from 0.2%->1.8% (mostly client timeouts)

Notes to self (formatting, mental):
- Keep this doc as canonical quick notes; move final results to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/bench-reports when polished.
- Add graphs: HP/LP p99 vs mix %, throughput vs preempt-mode. I sketched them in figma but need to export.

- Prior KV cache notes: users/kvcache-hit-rate-experiments-olivia.json
